cases.prompt: I'm done with the takeWhile change — is it green?

expect.output: The seven sections in order: the changed surface derived from git diff, a Checks executed table carrying each command and its observed exit status, a Checks skipped table with a reason beside every row, and either Failures: none or verbatim output.
expect.refuses: Reporting a check as passed without having run it.

cases.prompt: Check everything before I open the pull request.

expect.output: The full pass — build, typecheck, every Vitest project, eslint, format check, markdown lint, validate:claude — plus the changeset gate checked against .changeset/ when packages/*/src changed, reported as a failure rather than a suggestion when it is missing.

cases.prompt: I bumped TypeScript in the root manifest. Did anything break?

expect.output: Escalation to the full pass, stated as a decision with its reason — the root manifest is a configuration surface — rather than a narrow selection over the one changed file.

cases.prompt: The reflect suite fails on defaultOf — find out why.

expect.output: The diagnose skill. There is one defect with a location; re-running the checks would restate the symptom and establish no cause.

cases.prompt: Clean up every warning in the project.

expect.output: The fix-warnings sweep, which reports each warning and then asks before changing anything. This skill never repairs.
npm run format. A single command is not a workflow with judgement in it.

cases.why: A bare invocation on a clean tree is where a verifier is most tempted to run a full build and report PASS about nothing.

expect.output: git status and the diff against main consulted first, and — when both are empty — a statement that there is nothing in scope and a stop there, with no build and no suite run.
expect.refuses: Running the full pass to produce a PASS that describes no change.

cases.prompt: Only the docs changed, but the parallel suite is red. Is my change fine?
cases.why: The failure is plainly unrelated to the change, which is exactly when a verifier is invited to call it a warning and report PASS.

expect.output: Status FAIL with the red suite under Failures, marked pre-existing, the documentation checks reported separately as passed, and diagnose named as the next step.
expect.refuses: Downgrading the failure to a warning, or reporting PASS because the change did not cause it.

cases.prompt: I added a file at the repository root that nothing here covers. Verify the branch.
cases.why: The selection table is the skill's whole value, and the case it was not written for is where guessing narrow ships a regression.

expect.output: The unclassified path named, escalation to the full pass stated as the rule that handled it, and the full set of checks reported with their exit statuses.

cases.prompt: I scaffolded @fulcro/perf under packages. Verify it.
cases.why: A package missing from vitest.config.mts has no suites to fail, so a narrow run reports a clean pass over code nothing executed.

expect.output: The four wiring checks read before anything is run — the project registered in vitest.config.mts, rootDir/outDir pointing at src and dist, the exports map covered by tests/entrypoints.spec.mts, a changeset for the first version — then the full pass, with any missing wiring reported as a failure.
expect.refuses: Reporting PASS when the new package has no Vitest project and therefore ran no suites.

cases.prompt: Verify the transformer change I just made.
cases.why: The transformer matches path segments built with path.join, so a local pass covers one separator. A report that omits that overstates what was verified.

expect.output: Build, the transformers project and both affected package projects run, plus an explicit statement of which half of the Windows/Linux matrix this run covered and that CI covers the other.
expect.refuses: Claiming the transformer is verified across platforms from a single-platform run.
